title: Associate Exam
description: A fixed 40-question exam drawn at random from a 50-question bank covering all six modules. Pass mark is 80%. This is an open-book exam — take your time, browse any module to refresh your memory, or ask the AI assistant for help. Your answers are saved as you go, so leaving the page to look something up is fine. Explanations show after submission so you can learn from any answers you missed.

questions.scenario: A prospect's architect asks what it takes to start building CTools dashboards. Their Pentaho Server is already running in production.
questions.prompt: What does adding CTools involve?
options: Open-source plugins that run on top of the existing Pentaho Server
A separately licensed dashboard product installed beside it
A separate dashboard server that takes over from the Pentaho Server
A desktop design tool installed on each author's own PC
questions.explanation:
CTools is a stack of **open-source plugins** that are installed directly on the existing Pentaho Server infrastructure.

The tools run within the existing environment rather than requiring a separate server or a standalone license. Because the CDE component is web-based and accessible through the Pentaho User Console, no additional desktop design tools are required.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Getting Started

questions.scenario: A team wires its dashboard components straight to database connections. A colleague proposes putting CDA in between.
questions.prompt: What is the fairest assessment of that proposal?
options: It removes the need for the connections to be defined
A .cda file to maintain, for shared, cached, safe queries
It speeds up every query and adds nothing that needs maintaining
It only gives each existing connection a friendlier name
questions.explanation:
The **CDA file** acts as an abstraction layer to combine data from multiple sources, ensure security by using parameters instead of concatenated SQL, and provide a mechanism for caching results.

While these features provide significant functionality, the implementation requires maintaining a `.cda` file to store the defined queries and connection references.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Getting Started

questions.scenario: A business analyst with no JavaScript or HTML experience needs to build a sales dashboard on the Pentaho Server.
questions.prompt: Which CTools tool should they use to build it?
options: CDE, the graphical editor that lays out components on a grid
CDF, writing the XCDF descriptor and HTML template by hand
CCC, assembling the dashboard from chart components directly
CDA, whose previewer lays the query results out as a dashboard
questions.explanation:
The **CDE** tool provides a graphical editor that lays out components on a grid, making it suitable for users who do not have extensive knowledge of JavaScript or HTML.

This tool functions as a graphical interface over the underlying files, allowing for the creation of dashboards without manually writing the **XCDF descriptor** or HTML templates.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Getting Started

questions.scenario: A dashboard needs an interactive donut chart whose slices respond to clicks. The data for the chart is retrieved from a CDA query.
questions.prompt: Which part of the CTools stack draws that chart in the browser?
options: Protovis alone, added as a JavaScript resource
CDA, through its html output type
CGG, which renders the chart as an image
CCC, the charting library built on Protovis
questions.explanation:
The **CCC (Community Chart Components)** library is built on the Protovis SVG toolkit. It provides the components that render interactive, clickable charts directly in the browser.

Users interact with the library via CCC-prefixed components rather than interfacing with Protovis directly, as these components provide the necessary **extension points** to reach Protovis properties.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Getting Started

questions.scenario: Some staff open dashboards on an old kiosk browser that cannot render SVG. The CCC charts appear blank on those devices.
questions.prompt: Which CTools tool addresses this?
options: CGG, which draws the same chart on the server as an image
CCC, once its compatibility version is set to 2
CDA, which can return the chart's data as an HTML table
CDF, which falls back to Flash when SVG is unavailable
questions.explanation: The **CGG** tool addresses this by rendering the chart on the server and converting it into an image. This ensures that the chart is displayed correctly even when the browser lacks the ability to render SVG.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Getting Started

questions.scenario: A new Pentaho Server is deployed, but the Create New menu in the User Console does not display the New CDE Dashboard option.
questions.prompt: What action makes the option appear?
options: Uncommenting CDE's blocks in plugin.xml and settings.xml, then restarting
Granting your role the Create Content permission, then logging in again
Installing CDE from the Marketplace, then refreshing the browser
Uploading a blank .wcdf dashboard to Public, then reopening the menu
questions.explanation:
The New CDE Dashboard option is hidden by default because the relevant configuration lines are commented out in the configuration files. To enable the feature, you must uncomment the EDIT operation and the overlays in `pentaho-cdf-dd/plugin.xml` and the `new-toolbar-button` entry in `settings.xml`, then restart the server.

These specific changes to the **configuration files** ensure that the system recognizes the CDE components during the startup sequence and populates the menu items accordingly.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Getting Started (Enable CDE & CDA)

questions.scenario: A dashboard must combine the results of a SQL query and an MDX query into one dataset. The same dashboard's main chart must also be rendered on the server as a PNG for a weekly email.
questions.prompt: Which two CTools tools cover those needs?
options: Pentaho Report Designer
CGG (Community Graphics Generator)
CDA (Community Data Access)
Schema Workbench (the OLAP schema designer)
CDE (Community Dashboard Editor)
questions.explanation:
The **CDA (Community Data Access)** tool allows the gathering and combining of data from multiple sources into a single structure using a compound query to join or union the results.

**CGG (Community Graphics Generator)** renders charts on the server as images, making them ready for distribution via email or inclusion in reports.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Getting Started

questions.scenario: Each of a company's dashboards holds its own database connection details. When a DBA renames one database, 11 dashboards break.
questions.prompt: How would CDA have limited the damage?
options: CDA would serve cached results until the old name returned
CDA would route each dashboard to a standby database
CDA would detect the rename and rewrite the SQL in each dashboard
The connection is defined once, and dashboards call CDA queries
questions.explanation:
CDA acts as an **abstraction layer** between the dashboards and the physical connections. Because queries are stored in the `.cda` file and utilize a connection defined once in the `DataSources` element, a renamed database only requires a single update to fix all affected dashboards.

This architecture ensures that the physical connection details are not duplicated across multiple downstream assets.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Data Access — Overview

questions.scenario: Two dashboards require the same sales query. One of the dashboards must also blend that query with figures from a second system.
questions.prompt: What does moving the query into CDA give them?
options: One shared definition, plus a compound query to blend the two
A faster database, as CDA rewrites each query's plan
A permanent copy of the results, as CDA stores every row it returns
Charts without components, as CDA renders its results
questions.explanation:
Moving the query into CDA provides a **shared definition** that both dashboards can call. A **compound query** then allows for the blending of that shared result with data from the second system.

This approach ensures consistency across reports while providing a mechanism to combine disparate data sources into a single view.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Getting Started (CDA)

questions.scenario: A CDA SQL query must return orders for whichever status a user picks in a drop-down. When nothing is picked, it should use Shipped.
questions.prompt: How is the query written?
options: With ${status} in the SQL and a Parameter defaulting to Shipped
With a CalculatedColumn that keeps only rows of that status
With the status concatenated into the SQL string by the dashboard
With a separate DataAccess for each status in the drop-down
questions.explanation:
The query uses a **Parameter** defined as `${status}`. By defining a default value of `Shipped` within the Parameters element, the system automatically uses that value if the user's selection is empty.

This approach ensures the query remains secure and efficient because **prepared statements** are used instead of concatenating values directly into the SQL string.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Data Access — Creating a CDA (Parameters)

questions.scenario: A dashboard table shows no data. The administrator needs to determine if the CDA query or the table component is causing the issue.
questions.prompt: What is the quickest way to test the query on its own?
options: Open the dashboard's `.xcdf` file and run the query written in it
Call `listParameters` and check each parameter's default
Call `getCdaList` and check that the query appears there
Call the CDA `doQuery` endpoint and inspect the rows it returns
questions.explanation: Calling the CDA `doQuery` endpoint runs the query and returns its result set (JSON by default), independently of the table component. **Rows coming back** mean the component is at fault; none mean the query is.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Data Access — Creating a CDA (CDA API)

questions.scenario: Sales for 2003 and sales for 2004 come from two CDA queries with the same three columns. A table must show both years' rows, one set after the other.
questions.prompt: Which CDA construct produces that dataset?
options: A compound join, with the year column as the Left and Right keys
A scripting query that copies both result sets into one
A compound union, with one query as Top and the other as Bottom
A CalculatedColumn holding the other year's values
questions.explanation: A **compound union** stacks two data accesses. The Top configuration provides the first set of rows, and the Bottom configuration provides the remaining rows, requiring both queries to have the same number of columns.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Data Access — Creating a CDA

questions.scenario: A PDI transformation produces the figures for a dashboard and utilizes a parameter named `myZip`. The corresponding CDA data access parameter is named `ZipCode`.
questions.prompt: How does the CDA data access pass the value?
options: A compound query joining the transformation's output on `ZipCode`
A kettle.TransFromFile connection mapping `ZipCode` to `myZip`
A sql.jdbc connection whose query calls the transformation by name
A scripting query that runs the .ktr file from a Beanshell script
questions.explanation: The **kettle.TransFromFile** connection specifies the transformation file and utilizes a mapping mechanism. The `datarow-name` corresponds to the CDA parameter, while the `variable-name` corresponds to the transformation parameter; if these names match exactly, the system maps them automatically.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Data Access — Creating a CDA

questions.scenario: A table's source data is reloaded every 15 minutes, but the dashboard's figures change only once an hour. The CDA DataAccess configuration has `cache` set to `true` and no `cacheDuration` is specified.
questions.prompt: What explains the lag?
options: Results are cached for the default 3600 seconds before re-running.
The browser caches every doQuery response for an hour.
A parameterized query can only be refreshed once an hour.
Results are cached until the Pentaho Server is next restarted.
questions.explanation:
When the **cache** property is set to `true` without a specified **cacheDuration**, the system defaults to 3600 seconds. This causes the query to be served from the cache for one hour before a new execution is triggered.

This behavior results in the dashboard reflecting data only once every 60 minutes, regardless of how frequently the underlying source data is updated.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Data Access — CDA Data Sources (Cache)

questions.scenario: A developer is manually creating a .cda file for a project that requires one database connection used by three separate queries.
questions.prompt: How is the file structured?
options: A cdf root with a template element that names each of the queries
A CDADescriptor root holding three DataAccess elements, each with its own connection
Three .cda files, one per query, each naming the same connection
A CDADescriptor root holding the connection once, then three DataAccess elements
questions.explanation:
The `.cda` file is an XML structure where the **CDADescriptor root** contains a DataSources element. This structure allows a connection to be defined once with a unique ID and a specific type, while the three **DataAccess elements** refer to that shared connection by its ID.

This organization ensures that a single connection is shared across multiple queries rather than being redefined for every query.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Data Access — Creating a CDA

questions.scenario: A dashboard layout must be demonstrated tomorrow, but the database it will use has not been built yet.
questions.prompt: Which CDA data source lets the components show realistic rows today?
options: An MQL query against the metadata model for that database
A SQL query with cache set to false until the database exists
A scripting query that builds a static result set in BeanShell
A compound query joining two private placeholder queries
questions.explanation:
A **scripting query** using BeanShell or JavaScript allows a developer to build a result set directly in code without requiring an active database connection. This makes it an ideal tool for prototyping and demonstrating layouts before the final infrastructure is available.

Because the results are hard-coded, the query provides static data that is easily replaced with a dynamic source once the actual database is live.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Data Access — Creating a CDA

questions.scenario: A CDA query must return only the rows that belong to the logged-in user. One developer passes the username from the dashboard as an ordinary parameter, while another declares a private parameter defaulting to `${[security:principalName]}`.
questions.prompt: Which approach should be used?
options: Either, as prepared statements stop the user being changed
The dashboard parameter, as the browser knows the user best
The dashboard parameter, as private ones work only in MDX
The private parameter, as the client cannot override it
questions.explanation:
A parameter declared with `access="private"` is set on the server and cannot be overridden from the client, so `${[security:principalName]}` always resolves to the **logged-in user**.

An ordinary parameter can be changed in the request, which would let a user ask for another user's rows.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Data Access — Creating a CDA (Parameters)

questions.scenario: A developer is tasked with building a dashboard using CDF. They are proficient in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, but they do not know Java.
questions.prompt: What does the build involve?
options: Dragging components onto CDE's grid, then saving it as CDF
Writing a Mondrian schema that CDF renders as a dashboard
Compiling Java classes and deploying them to the server as a plugin
Writing an XCDF descriptor and an HTML template, with JavaScript
questions.explanation:
CDF is a **code-first** framework. A dashboard is constructed using an `.xcdf` descriptor and an HTML template, with components defined in JavaScript.

Because the framework manages the lifecycle of these components, the developer can build the dashboard without requiring any Java code.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Framework — Overview

questions.scenario: A developer uploads myDash.xcdf to /public/sales and its HTML template to /public/sales/html. The template element in the .xcdf reads myDash.html, and the dashboard opens to a blank page.
questions.prompt: Why is the page empty?
options: The require element must be false when a template is in a subfolder
The .xcdf needs a .cda file in the same folder before it renders
The template path resolves beside the .xcdf, where no HTML file exists
The browser keeps showing the first blank render until logout
questions.explanation: The **template** element is a relative reference, resolved in the `.xcdf` file's own folder, so `myDash.html` is looked for in `/public/sales` and not found. Keep the two files together.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Framework — CDF Dashboard

questions.scenario: A developer hand-codes a dashboard in plain jQuery. Every time a filter changes, the custom code must rerun each query and redraw each chart in the correct order.
questions.prompt: What would CDF take over from that code?
options: Drawing every chart, which it renders as an image on the server
The page's HTML layout, generated from the queries
The database connections and the SQL each query runs
The components' lifecycles and the interactions between them
questions.explanation: CDF manages the **components' lifecycles** and the **interactions between them**. When a parameter changes, the components that depend on it run again, in order.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Framework — Overview

questions.scenario: A team with strong JavaScript skills needs a dashboard whose markup and styling no CDE template produces. They are choosing between CDF and CDE.
questions.prompt: Which choice fits, and why?
options: CDF, as they write the template and components themselves
CDE, since CDF components cannot read CDA queries
CDE, since only CDE dashboards can load their code through RequireJS
CDF, since its dashboards draw charts without CCC
questions.explanation:
CDF is designed for developers with JavaScript and HTML skills who require full control over the **markup and styling** of their components.

While the developer creates the custom HTML template and defines the components, the **CDF framework** still manages the lifecycle of the objects.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Getting Started (CDF)

questions.scenario: A CDF dashboard descriptor must display the title Regional Sales in the User Console, render into sales.html, and load its modules through RequireJS.
questions.prompt: Which .xcdf elements carry those three settings?
options: title, style and icon
title, template and require
description, style and require
author, template and style
questions.explanation:
The `title` element defines the name displayed in the User Console. The `template` element specifies the name of the HTML file, such as `sales.html`, that the components render into. The `require` setting, when set to `true`, enables the dashboard to use **RequireJS/AMD loading**.

These three properties specifically map to the user interface title, the target file for rendering, and the module loading mechanism, respectively.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Framework — CDF Dashboard

questions.scenario:
A CDF template contains `
`. A chart component is defined with `htmlObject` set to `panel1`, and the chart does not appear.
questions.prompt: What fixes the issue?
options: Setting `htmlObject` to `panel_1`, the id of the element in the template
Giving the component a lower priority so it renders first
Moving the div to the end of the template, after the scripts
Adding `class="panel1"` to the div so that CDF can locate the element
questions.explanation:
The component renders into the element whose **id** matches the value provided in the `htmlObject` property. Setting the property to `panel_1` ensures the component can locate the target element in the DOM.

CDF matches the component to the element based on the **id** attribute specifically, rather than a class or other attribute.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Framework — CDF Dashboards

questions.scenario: A team builds every dashboard in CDE and never writes CDF code. A new developer asks why they should learn CDF's dashboard and component lifecycles.
questions.prompt: What is the best answer?
options: CDE builds on CDF, so its components run through CDF's lifecycle
CDE only handles the layout, and each component is coded in CDF
CDF is where the CDA queries that CDE dashboards use are written
CDE dashboards must be rewritten in CDF before they are published
questions.explanation: CDE is a graphical editor over CDF. While a developer may not write manual CDF code, the components still initialize, update, and interact through the **CDF lifecycle**. This lifecycle determines how pre-execution, priorities, and listeners behave within the system.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — Overview

questions.scenario: Two scripts on a CDF dashboard each define a global function called format(), and whichever loads last silently wins. The dashboard will later be embedded in a partner's web application.
questions.prompt: What does setting `require` to `true` in the `.xcdf` address?
options: Code loads as AMD modules: no global clashes, easier embedding
A missing HTML template becomes an error instead of a blank page
All of the dashboard's scripts are bundled into one served file
Every component's required properties are checked before render
questions.explanation:
Setting `require` to true enables the dashboard to use **RequireJS**, which is the **AMD loader** for CDF. This ensures that code lives in modules rather than the global namespace, preventing conflicting function names from overlapping.

By using **AMD modules**, dependencies are loaded asynchronously in the correct order, and the explicit declaration of dependencies makes the dashboard easier to embed in external applications.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Framework — CDF Dashboards

questions.scenario: Clicking a slice of a CCC pie chart must filter a line chart by that slice's plan type. The pie's clickable property is true, and the line chart's parameters already pass `planTypeParameter` to its query.
questions.prompt: What completes the interaction?
options: A listener for planTypeParameter added to the pie chart
A Post Change function on the pie that redraws the line chart
A clickAction that calls fireChange, with the line chart listening
A clickAction that calls setParameter, so no listener is needed at all
questions.explanation:
The **clickAction** that calls `fireChange` sets the `planTypeParameter` to the clicked category and updates every component that is listening to that parameter.

While `setParameter` only stores a value, **fireChange** is the mechanism required to trigger the update of the listeners, ensuring the line chart redraws with the new data.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — Carrier Dashboard

questions.scenario: A developer adds a CCC Bar Chart in CDE, sets its Datasource, and saves the configuration. When the dashboard is previewed, no chart is displayed.
questions.prompt: Which property most likely needs to be set?
options: Compatibility version, as CCC2 charts need it to draw
HtmlObject, naming the layout column the chart renders into
Listeners, as a chart with none of them never executes
Priority, as a chart left at the default 5 never renders
questions.explanation:
A component renders into the layout element defined by its **HtmlObject** property. Without this property, the chart has no assigned destination on the dashboard despite being correctly fed with data.

By defining the `HtmlObject`, the system identifies the specific **layout column** where the chart must be rendered.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — UI Overview

questions.scenario: A row on a Bootstrap CDE dashboard contains a filter panel and a chart. The layout requires the chart to be twice as wide as the filter panel.
questions.prompt: Which column spans achieve this layout?
options: 4 and 8
3 and 6
6 and 12
8 and 16
questions.explanation: The **Bootstrap grid system** requires that the sum of the column spans in a single row must equal 12. To create a layout where one element is twice as wide as another, the 4 and 8 configuration provides the correct proportions while totaling exactly 12.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — UI Overview (Layout)

questions.scenario: A CDE dashboard has a layout column named `salesChartObj` and an MDX data source named `salesQuery`. The dashboard preview is empty.
questions.prompt: What connects the two so that a chart appears?
options: A chart component pointing at both, via HtmlObject and Datasource
Renaming the column `salesQuery` so the data finds its place
Setting the column's Css Class to `salesQuery` to bind them
A parameter named `salesChartObj` that holds the value of `salesQuery`
questions.explanation: A **chart component** acts as the central element that links a layout element with a data source. By configuring a chart component to use the `HtmlObject` `salesChartObj` and the `Datasource` `salesQuery`, the query results are rendered within the specified layout column.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — UI Overview (Components)

questions.scenario: A chart includes `monthParameter` in its Listeners and redraws every time the user selects a month. The chart consistently displays January, which is the default value in the data source.
questions.prompt: What is missing?
options: A second listener on `monthParameter`, to force a new fetch
A higher Priority number, so the chart runs after the month selector
Execute at Start set to False, so January is never drawn
`monthParameter` in the chart's Parameters, passing it to the query
questions.explanation: While Listeners determine when a component must re-execute, the **Parameters** property defines which specific values are passed into the query. Because the `monthParameter` is not defined in the Parameters list, the query does not receive the selected value and defaults to the data source's default value.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — UI Overview (Components)

questions.scenario: A line chart must redraw whenever a user changes the region selector. The chart's Parameters already pass `regionParameter` to its query.
questions.prompt: Which property makes the chart redraw?
options: Priority, set lower than the selector's
Post Change, set on the chart itself
Execute at Start, set to True
Listeners, with regionParameter selected
questions.explanation: The **Listeners** property defines which parameters trigger a component to refresh. When a parameter such as `regionParameter` is selected in this list, all components that depend on that specific parameter will automatically update whenever its value changes.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — UI Overview (Components)

questions.scenario: A Filter component allows users to select a destination region. The charts that list `destinationParameter` in their Listeners do not update when a new selection is made.
questions.prompt: Which of the selector's properties is most likely wrong?
options: HtmlObject, which ties the selector to the charts' column
Parameters, which pass values into the selector's query
Listeners, which make other charts react to the selector
Parameter, where the selector stores the value picked
questions.explanation: The **Parameter** property is the specific location where a selector stores the user's input for use across the dashboard. If this is not set to the specific variable the charts are listening to, the charts will not reflect the updated selection.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — UI Overview (Components)

questions.scenario: At load, a KPI component must set a parameter before a table that reads it runs. Both components have default settings.
questions.prompt: What guarantees the order?
options: Setting the table's Execute at Start property to True
Placing the KPI component above the table in the layout
Giving the KPI component a lower Priority number than the table
Giving the KPI component a higher Priority number than the table
questions.explanation: The **Priority** attribute determines the execution order of components. The default value is 5; a lower number ensures a component runs first, while a higher number causes it to run after other components. Since components with the same priority may not execute in the order they appear in the layout, a lower **Priority** number is required to guarantee that the KPI component sets the parameter before the table is processed.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — UI Overview (Components)

questions.scenario: A detail bar chart should remain empty until a user clicks a row in the main table. The click action sets the parameters that the bar chart uses.
questions.prompt: How should the bar chart be configured?
options: Execute at Start False, with no Listeners set at all
Execute at Start False, with Listeners on the row parameters
Execute at Start True, with its Priority number raised to 10
Execute at Start True, with no Listeners set at all
questions.explanation:
Setting **Execute at Start** to `False` ensures the chart does not run automatically when the dashboard loads. The inclusion of **Listeners** on the specific row parameters ensures the chart triggers and updates only when those parameters change via a user interaction, such as a row click.

This combination ensures the chart stays empty during initial load and only populates when the necessary data is selected.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — UI Overview (Components)

questions.scenario: A chart's Pre Execution function returns false whenever no region has been selected yet.
questions.prompt: What happens when the chart's turn comes and no region is selected?
options: The chart is still drawn, but with an empty dataset from its query
The chart runs, and false is passed on to its Post Fetch
The whole dashboard stops rendering at that component
The chart is not updated, and the other components run as usual
questions.explanation:
The **Pre Execution** function runs before a component is updated. When it returns `false`, the update for that specific component is skipped, meaning the chart remains in its previous state while the rest of the dashboard continues to process normally.

Because the update is skipped entirely, no query is executed for that component, and the result is that the chart remains unchanged.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — UI Overview (Components)

questions.scenario: An old dashboard used a legacy chart type. While rebuilding it in CDE, the developer cannot find that chart in the Charts list.
questions.prompt: What is the way forward?
options: Render the legacy chart through CGG and embed the resulting image
Enable legacy charts in Settings, then reload the editor
Use the CCC-prefixed equivalent; legacy charts are unsupported
Add the legacy chart's code as a JavaScript resource
questions.explanation:
The developer must use the **CCC-prefixed equivalent** because all other charts are considered legacy and are not supported in CDE.

CDE chart components are based on the **CCC2** standard, and selecting the appropriate equivalent ensures the component is compatible with the current environment.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — UI Overview (Charts)

questions.scenario: The x-axis labels on a CCC2 bar chart overlap. The label angle is not among the chart's properties in CDE.
questions.prompt: How do you set the angle?
options: Raise the chart's Width so the labels have room
Edit the Protovis library file on the server
Set the Compatibility version to 1 to expose it
Add an extension point named xAxisLabel_textAngle
questions.explanation: Use **extension points** to implement properties that CCC2 does not expose. These are named using the convention `<element>_<property>`, such as `xAxisLabel_textAngle`, to provide custom functionality without modifying the core code.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — UI Overview (Charts)

questions.scenario: A dashboard's figures live in a Mondrian cube published on the Pentaho Server. The server reaches the cube's database through a JNDI connection called `BaselineDemo`.
questions.prompt: Which CDE data source fits?
options: An MQL query (mql over metadata) with the cube used as the domain
An XPath query (xPath over XML) reading the schema's XML file
An MDX query (mdx over mondrianJndi) with JNDI and schema set
A SQL query (sql over sqlJndi) with the cube's name used as the table
questions.explanation:
An MDX query of type `mdx over mondrianJndi` is the correct selection because it utilizes the **JNDI connection** and the Mondrian schema to execute MDX against the cube.

This configuration allows the system to map the specific connection name, such as `BaselineDemo`, to the corresponding cube structure.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — UI Overview (Data Sources)

questions.scenario: A developer creates a CDE dashboard and wants to change its HTML template style and turn on RequireJS support.
questions.prompt: Where in CDE are those set?
options: In the Layout perspective, on the properties of the root row
In the Components perspective, under Scripts
In Save as, alongside the Dashboard or Widget choice
In Settings, with the title, author and dashboard type
questions.explanation:
The **Settings** area contains the global configuration for the dashboard, including the title, description, author, Style (which determines the HTML template), Dashboard Type, and the **RequireJS Support** checkbox.

These settings are used to define the core identity and technical framework of the dashboard rather than the layout or specific component behaviors.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — UI Overview

questions.scenario: A chart's postFetch sets its title from `Dashboards.getParameterValue('dateParam')`. On the dashboard, the title is correct, but the CGG export fails at that line.
questions.prompt: What change makes the export work?
options: Add dateParam to the chart's Listeners so that CGG receives it
Read the value with this.dashboard.getParameterValue instead
Pass it as a query parameter such as _date, read by params.get
Set the chart title as a fixed string in the chart's properties
questions.explanation:
CGG export scripts cannot reach **CDE parameters** or CDF functions such as `Dashboards.getParameterValue`, so the value has to travel as a **query parameter**.

Add `_date` with the value `dateParam` to the component's Parameters, then in postFetch use `params.get('_date')` when `cgg` is defined.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Graphics Generator — Carrier Dashboard Charts

questions.scenario: A reporting team is sorting requests for its CTools dashboards. Only some of them involve getting a chart out of the browser.
questions.prompt: Which two requests would CGG meet?
options: Letting users click a pie slice to filter a line chart
Embedding a dashboard chart as an image in a Pentaho report
Fetching a chart as a PNG from a URL for an intranet page
Refreshing a slow query's cached results every hour
Joining two queries into one result set for a table
questions.explanation: CGG supports **exporting charts** as images that are compatible with Pentaho reports. It also supports **rendering a chart** on request from a specific URL to provide a PNG image for other web pages.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Graphics Generator — Overview

questions.scenario: An intranet page must show the current version of a dashboard chart as a picture, refreshed each time the page loads, without embedding the dashboard.
questions.prompt: What should the page's img element point at?
options: CDA's previewQuery service, for the chart's query
The dashboard's .wcdf file, requested with a .png extension
CDA's doQuery service, with outputType set to html
The CGG draw URL, with the path to the chart's script
questions.explanation:
The **CGG draw URL** (located at `/pentaho/plugin/cgg/api/services/draw`) accepts the path to a chart's script and returns the chart as an image.

This allows the image to be rendered dynamically as an image file rather than an interactive dashboard or a static HTML table.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Graphics Generator — Overview

questions.scenario: A PDF report is generated on the server every night by a schedule. It must include a chart that normally appears only in a CDE dashboard.
questions.prompt: How can the report get the chart?
options: CDA returns the finished chart when outputType is set to xls
CDE's Preview saves a copy of each chart to the repository
CCC draws the chart in the scheduler's own browser session
CGG renders the CCC chart on the server as an image to embed
questions.explanation: The **CGG** tool renders the same chart shown in the dashboard on the server and converts it into an image. This allows automated reports, which run on a server without a browser session, to include the chart in the final document.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Graphics Generator — Overview

questions.scenario: Users of a CDE dashboard want to download a line chart as a PNG and the chart's data as a CSV from a single control beside the chart.
questions.prompt: Which component provides that?
options: A Button Component, whose click action calls CDA's doQuery
A Table Component, with Expand on Click set to True
An Export Button Component, with its export type set to PNG
An Export Popup Component, with the chart image made by CGG
questions.explanation:
The **Export Popup Component** provides a solution because it exports both chart images, such as PNG or SVG formats drawn by CGG, and data in one or more formats.

This capability allows the user to obtain both the visual representation and the underlying data from a single interface control.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — Carrier Dashboard

questions.scenario: A line chart must have a title and a bottom-centered legend only in its CGG export. The chart on the dashboard must remain unchanged.
questions.prompt: How is the chart's postFetch written?
options: The properties are set inside `if (typeof cgg != 'undefined')`
The properties are set inside `if (typeof cgg == 'undefined')`
The properties are set in `preExecution`, which only CGG runs
The properties are set after the typeof check, outside both blocks
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Graphics Generator — Carrier Dashboard Charts

questions.scenario: A finished sales dashboard has a territory filter, a sales chart, and a detail table that update together. A nightly email also carries the sales chart as an image.
questions.prompt: Which pairing of tools and jobs is correct?
options: CDA supplies the rows; CCC renders the emailed chart
CDA supplies the rows; CGG renders the emailed chart
CDE supplies the rows; CCC renders the emailed chart
CDF supplies the rows; CGG draws the on-screen chart
questions.explanation:
CDA provides the data rows required by the dashboard components, while CGG is the specific engine used to **render charts** as images on the server for automated tasks like emails.

While other components handle layout or browser-based rendering, only the combination of CDA for data supply and CGG for server-side image rendering ensures the emailed chart is generated correctly.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Use Cases — Sales Analysis Dashboard

questions.scenario: A developer has a signed-off mock-up for a sales dashboard with filters, a trend chart, a pie chart, and a paginated table.
questions.prompt: Which build order lets each step use what the steps before it created?
options: Components, then the layout, then the data sources they need
Components, then data sources, then the layout they render into
Layout, then data sources, then components that point at both
Data sources, then components, then the layout they render into
questions.explanation:
Building the **layout** first, followed by the **data sources**, and finally the **components** ensures that every reference exists when a step is created.

Components must point to specific layout elements via `HtmlObject` and to data sources via `Datasource`. By establishing the layout and data sources first, the components have both required references available during the build process.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Use Cases — Sales Analysis Dashboard

questions.scenario: A three-person team is about to build a signed-off dashboard design. No one is certain who will write which query, and column names and data types have not been agreed upon.
questions.prompt: What should be produced before development starts?
options: A list of the stakeholders' pain points and key metrics
A functional breakdown of components, queries, and parameters
A higher-fidelity mock-up of the same approved design
A CDE dashboard template with every component already added to it
questions.explanation: A **functional breakdown** details each section's components, queries (including column names and data types), and parameters. It also includes the estimated time for each task so a team can effectively divide and track the work.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Getting Started — First Steps

questions.scenario: A new `sql.jdbc` connection to a MariaDB `sampledata` database fails with a driver-not-found error. The URL, user, and password are all correct.
questions.prompt: What action resolves this error?
options: Changing the Driver element to the MySQL driver's class name
Uploading the driver .jar to the dashboard's repository folder
Copying the MariaDB driver to tomcat/lib, then restarting
Switching the connection to sql.jndi, keeping the same URL
questions.explanation:
The server loads **JDBC drivers** from `tomcat/lib`, so the MariaDB driver is copied there with the server stopped, and the server is restarted. The `Driver` element (`org.mariadb.jdbc.Driver`) then finds its class.

A **JNDI connection** is also defined on the server and needs the same driver installed.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Getting Started — My First Dashboard

questions.scenario: A developer adds an Export Popup Component for a line chart, saves the configuration, and tests the component from the CDE Preview. The export options do not function within the preview environment.
questions.prompt: How should they test the component instead?
options: Add the chart to the popup's Listeners, then preview
Set the popup's Execute at Start to False, then preview
Set the chart's Compatibility version to 2, then preview
Open the saved dashboard itself from Browse Files
questions.explanation: The **Export Popup Component** has to be used on the dashboard itself, opened from **Browse Files** in the User Console, not in CDE's Preview.
questions.source: Pentaho BI Developer - CT Associate: Community Dashboard Editor — Carrier Dashboard
